summary: PR #9 adds a `--tab_length` option to the CLI (`markdown/__main__.py`), forwards it only when given, and documents it in the changelog and `docs/cli.md`. The change resolves issue #6 and leaves the no-option output unchanged. I found no blocker or major problems. Three minor points are noted below.
verified: Full suite: `python -m unittest discover tests` -> Ran 1183 tests, OK (skipped=52).

Changed modules: `python -m unittest tests.test_apis tests.test_cli_tab_length_ac` -> Ran 106 tests, OK. This includes the subprocess tests that run `python -m markdown --tab_length=2` and `--tab_length 2`.
flake8 on markdown/__main__.py, tests/test_apis.py, tests/test_cli_tab_length_ac.py -> no output (clean).
`parse_options(['--tab_length=2'])` and `parse_options(['--tab_length', '2'])` yield `tab_length: 2`; without the option the key is absent, so the default path is unchanged.

`markdown.markdown('- a

  - b
', tab_length=2)` nests `b` under `a`, which matches what the CLI option is meant to produce. `markdown.markdown(..., tab_length=-2)` and `tab_length=0` are forwarded the same way, so the CLI does not add new behaviour there.
`markdownFromFile(**kwargs)` passes kwargs to `Markdown`, which reads `tab_length` from kwargs (core.py:110), so the option reaches the library.
Diff touches only docs, `markdown/__main__.py` and tests; no CI files, no escaping or raw-HTML code paths changed.

Limits: Bash pipes, file writes under /tmp and `--help` were denied in this session, so the end-to-end CLI checks ran via the unit tests and direct `parse_options`/library calls rather than ad-hoc shell runs.

findings.issue: New test file duplicates the coverage of `TestCliTabLength` in tests/test_apis.py (same helpers, same inputs, same assertions) and is named and organised around internal acceptance-criterion IDs (`AC-FR-001-1`, `FR-00x`). Those IDs are pipeline artifacts that do not belong in the project's test layout.

The `--tab_length` help block in the docs was hand-written and may not match what optparse prints; the `--help` line in the code is 'Number of spaces per tab in the source. Defaults to 4.' Not verified against live `--help` output in this session because that command was denied.

No validation of non-positive values. `--tab_length=0` or `-2` is accepted and passed to the library, which then renders code blocks with odd indentation. This matches the library's own behaviour, so it is not a regression, but a maintainer may want a bounds check.
findings.evidence:
`markdown.markdown('- a - b ', tab_length=-2)` -> '
 a

 b
'; `parse_options(['--tab_length=-2'])` -> tab_length: -2.
